title: Lookarounds (Lookahead & Lookbehind)
description: Master zero-width assertions. Validate surrounding context with lookaheads and lookbehinds without consuming characters or including them in the match result.

primer.definition: Lookarounds inspect the text before or after the current position without 'consuming' characters into the match result. Positive lookahead (?=) and positive lookbehind (?<=) check for required presence; negative lookahead (?!) and negative lookbehind (?<!) check for required absence.
primer.goldenRule: Lookarounds are zero-width assertions: they assert conditions about adjacent text without advancing the regex matching engine's character index.
primer.mentalModel: Think of a lookaround as a security guard standing at a doorway (the current position in the string) who peers through a window to check what's on the other side, then reports pass/fail without ever stepping through. Lookahead peers forward, lookbehind peers backward, and either way the guard's own footprint never lands in the match — the checked text is inspected, not consumed.
points: Lookarounds are assertions, not captures: the text they inspect is never added to the overall match result, even though the engine reads it to decide pass/fail.
There are exactly four forms: positive lookahead (?=...), negative lookahead (?!...), positive lookbehind (?<=...), and negative lookbehind (?<!...).

Because lookarounds are zero-width, multiple lookaheads can be stacked at the same position (e.g. (?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)) to require several independent conditions without any of them advancing the match.

Lookbehind reads the text immediately before the current position; lookahead reads the text immediately after it — the direction is defined relative to the engine's current position, not relative to the rest of the pattern.
pitfalls: Lookarounds are zero-width and consume nothing: chaining several lookaheads at the same position (e.g. stacked password rules) is valid and common, but forgetting this leads to double-counting characters that were never actually part of the match.

Lookbehind patterns must be fixed-length or bounded in most JS-compatible engines — a variable-length quantifier like (?<=a+) inside a lookbehind is not universally supported, and relying on it can break across engines/environments.

It's easy to confuse direction: (?=...) and (?<=...) describe what surrounds the current position, not what's inside the overall match — beginners often expect the lookahead's content to appear in the captured text and are surprised when it doesn't.

Like ordinary literals, lookaround content is case-sensitive by default. A negative lookahead written to block a specific word (e.g. (?!temp\.com)) will silently let a differently-cased variant (TEMP.COM) through unless the pattern is normalized or the i flag is applied.

examples.note: Positive lookahead matches digits only when immediately followed by '%', but '%' itself is not part of the match.
Negative lookbehind matches digits only when NOT preceded by '$', so '$100' would not match at that position but a bare '100' would.
Two positive lookaheads stacked at the start assert both an uppercase letter and a digit exist somewhere in the string, without either lookahead consuming characters.

cards.prompt: Match 'foo' only if it is immediately followed by 'bar' using positive lookahead (?=...).
Match 'foo' only if it is NOT followed by 'bar' using negative lookahead (?!...).
Match 'bar' only if it is immediately preceded by 'foo' using positive lookbehind (?<=...).
Match 'bar' only if it is NOT preceded by 'foo' using negative lookbehind (?<!...).
Match lowercase letters only if followed by one or more digits strictly from start to end.
Match digits only if preceded by a dollar sign '$'.
Match price digits (with optional two decimal places) preceded by '$' without including '$' in match.
Match word key at line start only if followed by optional spaces and a colon.
Match integer digits strictly from start to end only if NOT ending with unit 'px'.
Match word 'admin' strictly at word boundary only if NOT preceded by 'super_'.
Extract string content inside angle brackets '<' and '>' using lookbehind and lookahead.
Validate full string contains at least one digit using positive lookahead strictly from start to end.
Validate full string contains at least one uppercase letter AND at least one digit strictly start to end.
Match filename strictly from start to end that does NOT end with executable extension '.exe' or '.bat'.
Match unescaped double quotes (a double quote NOT preceded by a backslash '\').
Match digit that is directly followed by multiples of 3 digits (used for comma separation in numbers).
Extract value of query parameter 'token=' from URL string using positive lookbehind.
Extract content strictly inside double quotes without including surrounding quotes using lookaround bounds.
Validate password: 8+ characters, at least 1 lowercase letter, 1 uppercase letter, and 1 digit strictly start to end.

testCases.description: Empty string fails every stacked lookahead plus the 8-character minimum.

cards.prompt: Match email address strictly from start to end, rejecting disposable domains '@temp.com' or '@disposable.org' via negative lookahead.

testCases.description: Negative lookahead is case-sensitive by default — an uppercase domain evades the block, same address as the failing case above except for letter case.

cards.prompt: Extract port digits preceded by 'localhost:' or '127.0.0.1:' using positive lookbehind.
Match word characters only if NOT preceded by '@' (to ignore social media mentions).
Extract 6-character hex color code digits preceded by '#' without including '#' in the match result.
Match API path starting with '/api/' but NOT matching deprecated versions '/v1/' or '/v2/' using negative lookahead.
